newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi troops kill five civilians-villagers say.
newsitem.headline: Burundi troops kill five civilians-villagers say.

text.p: Burundian troops killed at least five villagers on Tuesday south of the capital Bujumbura after clashing with Hutu rebels, villagers said on Wednesday.
They said troops killed the five villagers in hills ner Ruziba, seven km (four miles) south of Bujumbura, after Hutu rebels had terrorised the area, stealing cattle and food from peasants.

"An army patrol went up into the hills and met with rebels," a witness told Reuters. "But instead of engaging the rebels they killed innocent peasants." Army spokesmen were not immediately available to comment.
"They (soldiers) killed five people. We buried the bodies this morning," said another villager who declined to be named.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels since the killing of Burundi's first elected Hutu president in October 1993.

Julius Nyerere, the internationally-backed mediator on Burundi, announced in Dar es Salaam earlier on Wednesday that all party-talks aimed at resolving Burundi's civil war would start on August 25 in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha.
The talks would be the first public negotiations between the government of military leader Pierre Buyoya and the main Hutu rebel group the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD).
A representative of Buyoya, a retired army major who seized power in a coup a year ago, signed a pre-ceasefire agreement with the CNDD in April after months of secret talks in Rome.
